newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Sverdlovsk plans $100 million Eurobond.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Sverdlovsk plans $100 million Eurobond.

text.p: Russia's Sverdlovsk region plans to issue a $100 million Eurobond this year, and not one for $20 million as was previously announced, regional Governor Eduard Rossel said on Friday.
Rossel did not say exactly when the bond would be issued, but told Reuters Sverdlovsk expected to receive a credit rating from Standard & Poor's within two months.
Rossel said the $100 million issue would be the first of several over the next few years.
"We have signed an agreement with Inkombank about placing debt of (a total) $300 million with a maturity of six-seven years," he said.

Russia's AB Inkombank is financial adviser and co-manager on on the bond, which is being lead-managed by London investment bank WestMerchant Bank, a unit of Germany's Westdeutsche Landesbank Girozentrale (WestLB).
Sverdlovsk, based around the Urals city of Yekaterinburg, is one of several Russian regions and cities, including St Petersburg, Moscow and Nizhny Novgorod, planning Eurobond issues.
The issues are being held up by the government, which has yet to issue regulations outlining the taxation and financial terms of regional Eurobond issues.
